## Before you upgrade

- **Enter runs the search.** In the Search page's query box, Enter now runs the search and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) still runs it. With suggestions open, Tab takes the highlighted one, and Enter does once you moved to one with the arrow keys.
- **Splunk pack rules have high and critical severities.** security_content now gives nearly every TTP rule the same risk score, which made every one medium. TTP rules are now ranked by the ATT&CK techniques they detect: 77 critical (ransomware, wiping, exploitation of a named CVE), 196 high (credential theft, defenses disabled, lateral movement and the like), 492 medium. Anomaly rules stay low. Saved searches, dashboards and notifications that filter on severity may see more Splunk pack findings. See [Splunk security content](https://signalith.io/docs/detections/).
- **The Docker quick start runs the newest release.** Up to 0.3.1 it ran the image built from `main`, so a new install got unreleased code. It now runs the release named in `deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml`, and `git pull` moves it to each new release. To keep running the newest build of `main`, put `SIGNALITH_VERSION=main` in `deploy/docker/.env` before you `git pull`; do so if you updated from `main` after 0.3.1 came out, since going back to an older version isn't supported. See [Running another version](https://signalith.io/docs/docker/#running-another-version-or-building-the-image-yourself).
- **The Windows install line turns on process creation auditing.** Installing or re-running the Signalith Agent on Windows now turns on Audit Process Creation with the command line (Security event 4688), as the CIS benchmarks recommend, so the many rules that read program starts work without Sysmon. Add `-NoProcessAuditing` to the line to leave it as it is. See [Process creation auditing on Windows](https://signalith.io/docs/signalith-agent/#process-creation-auditing-on-windows).

## What's new

- **Turn on the Windows logs detections need from the install line.** With **Also turn on logs that are off by default** on **Add data** (`-EnableLogs`), the Windows agent's install line turns on PowerShell script block logging and the DNS client, Task Scheduler, CryptoAPI and device driver logs, which PowerShell and other rules read. Removing the agent turns off what it turned on. Script block logging records scripts with any password written into them. See [Logs that are off by default](https://signalith.io/docs/signalith-agent/#logs-that-are-off-by-default-on-windows). (BUY-04)
- **A starter set of detections.** Each pack card's one-click button now turns on about 140 high and critical rules that read only what hosts send as installed, instead of every high and critical rule. Browse rules marks the rules that need Sysmon, process auditing, PowerShell logging or the Linux audit log. See [The starter set](https://signalith.io/docs/detections/#the-starter-set).
- **The Docker quick start, locked to the release.** Each release now has `signalith-<version>-docker.tar.gz`: the quick start with Signalith's image locked to the digest the release built and signed, so it runs exactly that image and needs no `git`. See [The quick start locked to a release](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#the-quick-start-locked-to-a-release).
- **A failed Windows install or upgrade is undone.** If the `.msi` fails partway, a new install removes what it set up (services, the OpenSearch program, firewall rules; data is kept), and an upgrade puts the previous version back and starts it again, instead of leaving nothing installed. An OpenSearch upgrade whose service does not start goes back to the version before; one that starts but never answers is left for you to retry with the `.msi`. See [Install from packages](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#windows). (WIN-02)
- **The Windows installer downloads OpenSearch through a proxy.** It uses the computer's proxy setting (`netsh winhttp`), or `HTTPS_PROXY`, or one you name with `OPENSEARCHPROXY=host:port`, and checks there is room on the disk before the 1 GB download. A proxy that needs a password is not supported; use `OPENSEARCHZIP`. See [Install from packages](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#windows). (WIN-03)
- **Replace a cluster's certificate authority.** `signalith cluster tls rotate-ca` (also on the Servers page) replaces the CA in steps: prepare, switch, retire, with abort before the switch. While it changes, servers and agents trust both the old and the new CA, so nothing drops off. Agents report which CAs they trust, and the Endpoints page flags one that trusts a CA no server uses. See [Replacing the cluster's CA](https://signalith.io/docs/servers/#replacing-the-clusters-ca). (CTL-01)
- **A findings queue built for a team.** The queue sorts and pages on the server (200 at a time, sorted by urgency or time), filters to unassigned findings, keeps its filters in the link, and has A (assign to me) and R (resolve) keys. Each user can save filters as named views, and the queue can group findings by detection or entity. Each urgency has a pick-up and a resolve target (Settings > Detections), the queue shows when a finding is due or how late it is, and a rule can send a finding again when nobody picks it up in time. Resolving asks for a disposition, and a new Posture card ranks the noisiest detections by false positives. See [The findings queue](https://signalith.io/docs/detections/#the-findings-queue).
- **Analysts propose exceptions, admins approve them.** An analyst can propose an exception from a finding with the values, how long and why; an admin approves or declines it on the Approvals page, and requests expire after 14 days. See [Proposing an exception](https://signalith.io/docs/detections/#proposing-an-exception).
- **Exceptions for many detections at once.** An exception can cover every detection, a content pack's rules or a tag's, and a finding can add one ("Except this host from all rules"). See [Exceptions for many detections](https://signalith.io/docs/detections/#exceptions-for-many-detections). (DQ-09)
- **Content pack rules keep their author's credit in notifications.** Email, Slack and Teams messages about a pack rule's finding carry its credit line, and webhooks get `finding.credit`.
- **SigmaHQ pack: antivirus rules.** Six antivirus rules join the SigmaHQ pack, and its report now accounts for every rule in SigmaHQ's checkout, with why each left-out rule is left out. (DQ-06)

## Fixes

- **The network sensor installer no longer silently stops a Fluent Bit or Suricata already running.** If `fluent-bit.service` or `suricata.service` runs (or is enabled) for something else, it stops before changing anything and says how to go on: `--docker` leaves it alone, `--take-over` stops it and `--uninstall` starts it again. See [Network sensor](https://signalith.io/docs/network-sensor/). (DEP-05)
- A detection with no throttle window and a lookback longer than its schedule no longer raises a new finding for the same row on every overlapping run.
- In a cluster, a server whose job lease renewal was answered late no longer takes the lease back after it ran out, which briefly stopped jobs and refused tenants' requests.

**Search**
- `where a > b` compares two fields. A bare name on the right of a `where` comparison now names a field, as in Splunk: `where bytes_out > bytes_in` and `where failures > successes` compare the fields on each row that has them, where they compared with the text before and silently dropped or kept the wrong rows. On rows without such a field the name is still text. A search that meant the text should put it in double quotes, as in `where user="admin"`. (SL-02)
- **Weeks start on Sunday everywhere, and `earliest=` checks its time.** `earliest=-7d@w`, `bin span=1w` and `timechart span=1w` now all start weeks on Sunday, as Splunk's `@w` does; `bin` and `earliest=` used Monday and `timechart` used Thursday. `earliest=` and `latest=` read epoch times as seconds (they were milliseconds, so `earliest=1767225600` meant January 1970), accept chained modifiers such as `@d-1h`, quarters (`@q`) and `@w1` to `@w6`, and refuse a time they cannot read instead of returning nothing. A saved search with such a time now shows the error. See [Query language](https://signalith.io/docs/query-language/).
- `timechart ... by` picks its series over the whole range and counts each in every bucket, where a value outside one bucket's top 10 showed 0 there; it adds `OTHER` and `NULL` series as Splunk does (`useother=f`, `usenull=f` leave them out).
- Closer to Splunk: `sort 10 -count` keeps 10 rows and sort keys take `num()`, `str()`, `ip()` and `auto()`; a multivalue field matches `where` and `search` when one of its values does; `stats` and `top` by a multivalue field count each value; `values()` keeps up to 10,000 values with their types and marks the result truncated when it leaves some out.
- `stats sum(bytes*)` and `stats values(*) as *` cover every matching field, as in Splunk, where the pattern was read as one field's name and gave nothing; `timechart`, `chart`, `streamstats` and `by *` refuse a `*` field name instead of returning empty columns. New: `head limit=N`, `stdevp`, `varp` and `sumsq`, and the eval functions `sha512`, `random`, `pi`, `exact`, `isbool`, `ipmask`, `atan2`, `hypot` and the trigonometric functions.
- The Ask box no longer runs a query for a question it half understood: a word that made it into no filter, grouping or data model now counts as not understood ("accounts locked out today" read as `user=locked` with full confidence), and such a query waits for you to run it, or goes to the AI model when one is set up. It now knows account lockouts and the DNS, web, registry, intrusion detection, alert and certificate data.
- New page: [Splunk SPL compatibility](https://signalith.io/docs/compatibility/) lists the commands and functions that work as in SPL, the ones that work differently and the ones that are missing.
- Checked against Splunk with a new set of searches and their expected rows: `sort` puts upper case before lower case, `sum()` of a group with no numbers is empty instead of 0, and `top` gives `percent` to six decimal places.
- The Search page runs searches in your browser's time zone, shown next to the results: `@d` and the other snaps, `timechart` and `bin` days and weeks, `strftime` and `relative_time` follow it instead of UTC. Detections and dashboards still run in UTC.
- A result is marked **Sampled** when commands such as `eval`, `rename`, `bin` or `dedup` before `stats` ran over only the newest `search.max_events` events of more that matched, so its counts cover only those; Explain says so too. Backtests count such runs as capped.
- With more than 50,000 groups, `top`, `rare` and `stats ... | sort -count | head N` keep the largest groups (ranked in OpenSearch) instead of the first 50,000 by name, so the top rows are the right ones; such results show **Ranked**.
- Three searches that read back differently from how they were written are fixed: a bare name in `where` that needs quotes, a field name starting with `[`, and `timechart limit=10`.

**Signalith Agent**
- Fluent Bit's buffer on each computer is capped at 1 GB (4 GB on a network sensor). While Signalith cannot be reached the oldest events are dropped past that, rather than filling the computer's disk. Agents pick this up by themselves; a Fluent Bit you set up by hand gets it when you download its configuration again from **Add data**. (ASI-01)
- When Signalith refuses a computer's token three times in a row, the agent stops Fluent Bit and osquery instead of reading events Signalith would drop, and starts them again from where they were once the token is accepted. (ASI-01)
- An agent update now rolls back when the new version starts but cannot reach Signalith, not only when it fails to start. (ASI-04)
- The agent's service and osquery's on Linux may use at most 512 MB of memory each (two CPU cores for the agent, one for osquery), and each collector on Windows at most 512 MB. Run the install line again on a computer set up before to get them. (ASI-15)
- osquery's `curl` and `curl_certificate` tables are off on every host, and sending a live query asks for your password again when you have not entered it in the last 15 minutes. (ASI-12)

**Load balancers**
- The HAProxy and keepalived samples in `deploy/loadbalancer` now check `/readyz` for syslog too (over TLS, TCP and UDP), so a server that is starting, stopping, drained or cut off from OpenSearch gets no syslog from the balancer. Copy the new checks into a balancer set up from the old samples. See [Load balancers](https://signalith.io/docs/load-balancers/). (DEP-01)

**First hour**
- The Security page no longer says the built-in admin still has the Docker setup's first password after it was changed from the account menu. A server that shares its users with the cluster (the Docker quick start's too) now reads the password in use, the page checks again right after a change, and the fix points to **Change password** with no restart.
- A plain word in a search matches the start of a word that has dots or underscores in it, as in Splunk: `mimikatz` finds `mimikatz.exe`.
- The setup guide's security step is done only when nothing is at risk and nothing needs attention, as the Security page counts them; it said Done while the page listed things to fix.
- The Health page and the Health card say **OpenSearch refuses writes** when OpenSearch's disk is past its high or flood-stage watermark. The cluster stays green then, so Health said Healthy while new events, findings and detection runs failed. See [Data retention](https://signalith.io/docs/retention/#the-disk-guard).
- Loading the sample data runs the detections four at a time, which took a test load with 119 rules on from about 4 minutes to about 2. Rules turned on while the sample is loaded say that they only watch new events, and how to run them over the sample week. The Detection health card no longer counts a rule turned on less than 30 days ago as having no match in 30 days.
- The Windows agent collects the exploit protection log's user mode events (`Microsoft-Windows-Security-Mitigations/UserMode`) as well as its kernel mode ones, which the Sigma exploit protection rules read. Run the install line again on a computer set up before, or download the Fluent Bit or OpenTelemetry Collector configuration again from **Add data**.

**Compliance**
- The Compliance page shows evidence only for what Signalith observed. Built-in items count once events arrive, an empty findings queue or an unused feature is no longer evidence, clock-sync controls use the hosts' time-sync checks, plain syslog and retention without the data behind it show as partial, controls that ask for more than a SIEM can see say so and stay partial, and notes on controls are audited and no longer raise the score. See [Compliance](https://signalith.io/docs/compliance/). (COMP-01, 02, 04 to 07, 14)
- Controls a SIEM cannot show (PCI DSS 8.3.4, HIPAA risk analysis, SOC 2 CC4.1) are no longer listed, and eleven more say what they ask for beyond Signalith. (COMP-03)
- Sign-in and process logs count as evidence only when every computer running the agent or osquery sends them, and the evidence names those that do not. Configuration checks no longer count for hosts on a platform they do not cover, and checks that fail to run everywhere show as gaps. Reports and CSV exports name the mapping version, the Signalith version and who exported them, and say how each kind of evidence was measured. (COMP-08, 09, 11)

**Behavior baselines**
- Behavior baselines are quieter and sturdier. Data volume is judged against the same hour of the day too, so nightly backups and weekly syncs no longer add risk. A check whose search fails waits on its own while the others go on, a reset check learns the stored history again instead of starting from nothing, programs and kinds of change keep up to 2,000 values per user or host, and an hour's search reads up to 250,000 rows. See [Behavior baselines](https://signalith.io/docs/baselines/). (UEBA-01, 02, 03, 06, 07, 08)
- An admin can forget one value for one user or host, such as a country learned while an account was misused, with **Forget it** on the risk event, without resetting the check for everyone. A new or long-unused account's first sign-in from the internet now adds half the new-country risk instead of waiting out the learning period. (UEBA-04, 05)

**Shared detections**
- With `detections.sync: mirror`, a server whose detections or dashboards folder is found empty (or that would remove many shared files of one kind at once) no longer deletes the shared library on every server: it removes nothing of that kind, writes the files back, and says so in its log, the audit log and the Servers page. This guards against accidents, not against removals made a few files at a time. To allow one such removal, put a file named `allow-mass-delete` in that folder and remove the files within the hour. See [Servers](https://signalith.io/docs/servers/#shared-detections-dashboards-and-asset-lists). (CTL-04)

**Syslog**
- Syslog batches OpenSearch refuses for now (down, too busy, write block, 5xx, timeout) wait in a spool on the server's disk (`syslog-spool` in the state folder, 1 GB by default, `syslog.spool_mb`) and are written again, oldest first, once it takes writes, also after a restart. When the spool is full the oldest batches are dropped and counted; the Health page shows the spool and warns when it dropped events or is over half full. See [When OpenSearch is down](https://signalith.io/docs/sending-data/#when-opensearch-is-down). (SS-03)
- Syslog over TLS (port 6514) no longer sends TLS session tickets. A TLS 1.3 sender that never read them reset the connection when it closed, and lines it had not yet sent were lost. Syslog senders do not resume sessions, so nothing else changes.

**Servers**
- The OpenSearch card on the Servers page shows the shards in use against `cluster.max_shards_per_node`, and warns when OpenSearch holds, or at today's data models and retention will hold, 80% of the shards it allows, on one node too. When OpenSearch refuses a new day's index for lack of shards, the server log says so and senders are asked to send the events again instead of losing them. See [Server settings](https://signalith.io/docs/settings/). (SS-02)
- A server that just restarted no longer signs people out when it cannot read their session from OpenSearch for a moment: it tries again briefly, then answers `503` with `Retry-After`, and the page stays signed in. Signed-out, changed and ended sessions are refused as before. See [Users](https://signalith.io/docs/users/#when-opensearch-cannot-be-used).
- On the Servers page, a rule that ran late on one server no longer makes the server it moved to look like it is falling behind.

## Security fixes

- OpenTelemetry Collectors that send a batch again (after a 503, or an answer they never got) no longer store its log records twice: each record gets a document ID from the request, as agent and HEC batches do.
- Log records OpenSearch can only take later (it is too busy, or its disk is full) are now answered over OTLP with 503 and `Retry-After`, so the Collector sends them again instead of dropping them as a partial success.
- Syslog and auth.log lines, and CEF and LEEF records, whose time has no zone (RFC 3164's `Oct 11 09:15:02`) are no longer read in the server's time zone, which filed events from hosts in other zones hours off. They take the collector's time (Fluent Bit's `date`, the OpenTelemetry or HEC time, or when Signalith received them), and the time the host wrote is kept in `device_clock`. A time with a zone name Signalith doesn't know is no longer read as UTC or as the server's time. See [Ingest limits](https://signalith.io/docs/sending-data/#ingest-limits).
- The Security page's HTTPS check no longer says Good when a reverse proxy, even one on the same computer, takes sign-ins or agent events over plain HTTP: requests the proxy marks `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` are now counted, under the client's address.
- With HTTPS off and the web page on `127.0.0.1`, the HTTPS check now also looks at the agent address: an agent port other computers can reach over plain HTTP needs attention, and is at risk once agents send to it.
- Signalith now recognizes that it runs in a container in Kubernetes pods too (the Helm chart sets `SIGNALITH_CONTAINER=1`), so the Security page checks the pod's protections instead of asking for a systemd service, and the report names the deployment correctly.
- Triage of findings, investigation cases, detections and their exceptions are now written to the audit log, with what changed from and to, so the signed audit log shows who closed, suppressed or changed what. See [Audit](https://signalith.io/docs/audit/#triage-cases-detections-and-threat-intel).
- Threat intel changes (indicators added, deleted or uploaded, and feeds added, changed, deleted, tested or refreshed) are now written to the audit log, with a feed's address logged without its key.
- A manual or uploaded threat intel indicator can no longer be a network broader than /8 (IPv4) or /16 (IPv6), such as `0.0.0.0/0`, which would have matched nearly every event. Feeds already skipped these.
- Investigate with AI now guards the masked values themselves, not only the masked fields: when the model asks for a search with a value, wildcard pattern or free-text word that could match a masked value under any field name, the investigation stops without telling the model, so it can no longer probe a masked user name through another field such as `TargetUserName`. Regular expressions are no longer allowed in its searches, `where` may only compare a field with a value as written, not with another field, `<` and `>` work only on `_time` and on counts made by `stats` or `top`, and values may use only ASCII characters while some are masked. See [Investigate with AI](https://signalith.io/docs/investigate/).
- Threat intel feed addresses in logs and on the page for non-admins no longer keep a fragment (`#...`), which could hold a key.
- An error answer from the AI model's service is shown only when it is the service's own JSON error message; other text in its place is logged instead.
- An error on the server no longer shows its underlying cause, such as OpenSearch's address or a file path, to whoever made the request. The page says that something went wrong, with a short reference that an admin can find, with the details, in the server log.
- **One account can no longer sign everyone else out.** Each user keeps at most 50 sign-in sessions; a 51st ends that user's oldest, never another user's. Before, enough sign-ins by one account on a single server pushed out the sessions of every other user, admins included.
- **Windows: Signalith's own account no longer has access to OpenSearch's folder.** `C:\ProgramData\SignalithOpenSearch`, which holds the CA key and the admin certificate, gave `NT SERVICE\Signalith` full control. It is now SYSTEM and Administrators only (OpenSearch's own account keeps its settings, data and logs). Running the 0.3.2 installer fixes an existing install.
- **The NVD API key stays on its server.** It no longer follows a redirect to another server, and the NVD, KEV and EPSS downloads now go through the same checks as threat intel feeds, so they never reach this machine, Signalith's OpenSearch or a cloud metadata service. An NVD mirror on this machine needs `intel.allow_loopback_feeds`, as feeds do.
- **Approving a server means typing its fingerprint.** The Servers page and `signalith cluster approve <name>` at a terminal ask for the fingerprint the new server shows on its sign-in page or in its log, instead of a checkbox or a yes next to the fingerprint OpenSearch holds, which anyone who can write to OpenSearch could have made. Lists of waiting servers show only the first group of each fingerprint.
- **The audit integrity check catches deleted audit indices.** With every audit index, or every record in them, deleted, **Check integrity** and `signalith audit verify` reported a clean result. They now report the records removed when servers sign their records, also when other records were put in their place.
- **`signalith tls import` works again after `reset-key`.** A server rebuilt with a new key can import the cluster's certificate authority again instead of having to set the cluster up from scratch. (CTL-02)
- **Leaked signing keys can be revoked.** A new offline root key signs revocation lists. Servers download the list with the content bundle, remove a content update signed with a revoked key, refuse revoked agent updates and hand the list to agents. See [Key management](https://signalith.io/docs/key-management/).
- Exceptions made from a finding match its values exactly: a logged value such as a user named `*` no longer becomes a wildcard that silences every result with that field. (DQ-09)
- Built with Go 1.26.10, which fixes a standard library `crypto/x509` vulnerability reachable from certificate loading.
